notes: §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR7: 'there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked and had not yet returned control'; 1985 leaves such an execution undefined, so any outcome conforms provided the run neither recurses nor corrupts. DispatchEmitter#EmitRunUseBody emits the per-declarative __useActive guard; at --std 85 the group is EC-free (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION and EC-names are refused, COBOL0877/COBOL0878), so the void arm 'if (__useActive[__id]) return;' declines the nested invocation quietly. Probes: a READ past end inside the relative file's USE (status 46) and a failed OPEN INPUT inside an INPUT-mode USE (status 35) each return without re-entering the procedure, its counter staying at 1; the witness checks the single invocation on status 10.

next.reason: 1985: "there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked"; 2023: "if a statement raises an exception condition that would cause the execution of a USE procedure ... the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist". 1985 forbids such execution and leaves the result undefined. 2023 covers the same case and defines the effect: the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist.
